previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic gastrointestinal dysmotility, and a history of recurrent DVTs was admitted due to a subjective feeling of being unwell and unsteady, accompanied by episodes of involuntary head nodding. She expressed concern these symptoms might signal sepsis or a neurological malignancy, especially given her family history. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, normal labs, and no signs of infection at her G-tube or femoral line sites. Imaging showed bowel distention consistent with ileus but no acute obstruction. Two sets of blood cultures showed no growth. The head-shaking episodes were witnessed by the care team and determined to be non-epileptic, with the patient remaining alert and hemodynamically stable throughout. She was reassured, continued on all home medications including Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis, and discharged home with a planned neurology follow-up to evaluate the movement episodes and an outpatient biopsy for a benign-appearing abdominal nodule.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o F with multiple recent admissions and complex PMH who 
presents with left sided rib pain.  

# Abdominal Pain: Chronic pain. Seen in the pain clinic by Dr. 
___.  Is on a pain contract and receives a 
morphine suppository 30-mg to be taken
every 6 hours. This was continued on admission. Her history of 
normal bowel movements + flatus, normal G-tube functionality, 
normal imaging studies were reassuring.  During the morning, she 
began to complain of worsening of her chronic abdominal pain and 
adamantly demanded 1mg IV dilaudid. Stating that she would leave 
if she did not recieve the medicine. We contacted Acute Pain 
Service and asked about advisability of giving IV dilaudid for 
chronic abdominal pain. We were told that this would be 
contra-indicated as it could worsen GI motility and exacerbate 
her symptoms. We informed her that we were happy to continue the 
ketoralac, lidoderm patch and her home pain regimen, but would 
not be giving as IV dilaudid as it was not indicated at this 
time. At this point, the patient informed the team that she 
would like to leave. As she was admitted for rib pain and three 
days of ketorolac we felt that she was medically stable to go. 
She was offered prescription for lidoderm and acetominophen but 
deferred stating that they don't help. She was anxious to leave 
but appeared tearful and resentful about not recieving dilaudid.

# Rib pain - The patient's rib pain is of sudden onset and 
localizes relatively well over the 6th rib. She has a history of 
osteoporosis and is at risk of fracture. However, no displaced 
fractures were seen on CXR and it is unlikely that finding a 
small fracture would change overall management. The patient 
agreed that a CT scan would be a good thing to avoid as she has 
had many CT scans in the past. Could also consider MSK strain 
fro lifting this bag. She was started on the first day course of 
Toradol BID and given a lidoderm patch for pain. She was also 
continued on her home pain medication regimen and continued on 
calcium and vitD supplements. In the morning's exam, she was 
moving all extremities with no clear restriction, taking deep 
breaths easily. She was continued on her home pain medication as 
well.

difficulty with motility and obstructions in the stomach and 
upper small bowel. No medicine changes were made.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Chronic abdominal pain, now worse.  Evaluate for acute process.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to abdominal radiographs from ___ and
CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS:

3 frontal including upright views of the abdomen demonstrate air and stool
within the colon, which is not as dilated on the pior radiograph, as well as
redemonstration of air-fluid levels within the duodenum and proximal dilated
loops of jejunum in the left upper quadrant, as seen prevously on CT of the
abdomen and pelvis.   Multiple clips are again seen in the right upper
quadrant cm midline abdomen.  A left femoral catheter is unchanged in position
terminating in the mid IVC.  A spinal stimulator is again seen.  A coiled
drainage catheter is also seen overlying the left upper quadrant which appears
folded approximately 13mm from the port.  It is unclear whether this kink is
internal or external to the body of the patient.  There is no intraperitoneal
free gas or pneumatosis.  

IMPRESSION:

Dilated loops of small bowel with air fluid levels, similar in appearance to
prior CT of the Abdomen from ___.  Clinical correlation is recommend for
the need for further imaging.

HISTORY:  Left-sided rib pain.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Heart size is normal.  Mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged. 
Pulmonary vasculature is normal.  The lungs are clear. No pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is identified.  Percutaneous gastrostomy catheter and spinal
stimulator wires are again demonstrated.  A catheter is also noted projecting
over the right lung base, unchanged. Multiple clips are again seen in the
right upper quadrant.  No displaced fractures are identified.  

IMPRESSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary process.  No displaced fractures are seen.  If there
is continued concern for rib fracture, then a dedicated rib series is
suggested.
